head: f1607fe5
status: Review-only proposals; not canonical SEC snapshots

source.context: Liu et al. (2022); related Singh et al. (2022), 10.1016/j.xcrm.2022.100633. Preliminary source verification only; full appraisal not undertaken after ownership gate.

limitations.text: Canonical PM5 expressly excludes mitophagy and damaged-organelle removal. PM9 formation of new mitochondria is not equivalent to mitophagic removal.
Older-adult ATP-production and six-minute-walk primary comparisons were null; muscle endurance is not mitophagy flux.
Historical urolithin discussion and dietary metabolites do not constitute admission of this supplement protocol.

rationale.gate: Do not score a mismatched receiving operation or broaden its mission. Author must resolve ownership before further appraisal.

records.first_line: Eight-week endurance cycling → within-group increase in muscle mitochondrial respiration

source.context: Irving et al. (2015); 65 sedentary younger/older adults; ET n=22; biopsies 48 hours after training; assay-specific sample sizes.

limitations.text: Do not transfer combined-training versus control significance to endurance alone.
Small age subgroups, multiple substrates and variable biopsy availability.
Ex-vivo muscle respiration is not neuronal ATP supply or cognitive benefit.

rationale.B: Random allocation and supervised exposure; selected complete assays and multiple comparisons remain concerns.
rationale.P: Figure 1 reports SEM and tests, but causal endurance-control contrast remains insufficiently established for admission.
rationale.R: One independent dataset for this exact protocol; combined training reuses controls, not replication.

assessment_gaps.task: Resolve exact endurance-versus-control respiratory contrast and uncertainty before proposing a causal superiority admission. Existing score applies only to within-arm observation.
assessment_gaps.attempted: Primary Methods, Results and Figure 1 caption inspected; explicit control superiority concerns combined training.
assessment_gaps.dimension: Admission proposition; no missing numerical factor silently replaced with zero.

six_atoms.Intervention: Supervised cycling, approximately 65% VO2peak, 60 minutes five days/week for eight weeks; randomised nontraining control and resistance-training arms.

moa.description: Repeated contractile demand may remodel oxidative machinery; mediation was not isolated.
moa.status: Proposed relationship; measured endpoint does not establish causal mediation

Biological relationship.measuredEffect: State-3 respiration increased within the endurance arm; tissue complex I+II P=.059. Explicit superiority over control in the Results concerned combined training, not endurance alone.
Biological relationship.pmRelevance: Muscle ETC-linked oxygen flux is relevant; reduced electron leakage and brain effects were not measured.

records.first_line: Tested low-LA/high-EPA/DHA diet → higher circulating DHA-ethanolamide

source.context: Courville et al. (2023); 66 randomised women with overweight/obesity, 62 reached four weeks, 59 twelve weeks. First four weeks weight maintenance; subsequent intake permitted weight loss.

limitations.text: LA lowering and EPA/DHA addition are a combined exposure; not evidence that LA reduction alone causes benefit.
AEA was not lowered; within-arm AEA rose in both low-LA groups.
Power targeted fatty-acid composition; unbalanced allocation, recruitment stopped early and last measurements carried forward.
No inflammation, brain signalling or clinical efficacy claim.

rationale.D: Direct LC-MS/MS concentration endpoint for the tested diet.
rationale.B: Controlled feeding and masking support inference; secondary endpoint, attrition and imputation limit protection.
rationale.P: Adjusted contrasts narrow direction; magnitude and generalisability remain uncertain.
rationale.R: One controlled feeding dataset; related oil studies do not replicate this formulation.

six_atoms.Intervention: Twelve-week supplied diet: LA 1% energy, EPA .16% and DHA .38%; compare low-LA/low-n3 and high-LA/low-n3 diets.

moa.description: Dietary fatty-acid supply may alter ethanolamide substrate availability; synthesis flux and clearance were not separated.
moa.status: Proposed relationship; measured endpoint does not establish causal mediation

Biological relationship.measuredEffect: Adjusted DHA-ethanolamide was higher with high n3; within-arm increase 31%. AEA and 2-AG did not differ between diets.
Biological relationship.pmRelevance: DHA-derived ethanolamide availability fits this PM; plasma concentration is not production flux or CNS engagement.

records.first_line: Tested phenolic-rich olive oil → lower circulating oxidised LDL

source.context: Covas et al. (2006), EUROLIVE; 200 healthy men; randomised masked crossover; 18 noncompleters; mixed models checked period/carryover.

limitations.text: No claim of reduced inflammatory signalling or universal systemic antioxidant effect.
Defined oils; retail EVOO label does not guarantee tested phenolic concentration.
Short interventions in healthy men; diet self-report and co-food interactions remain limitations.

rationale.D: Direct assay of exact circulating oxidised-LDL proposition.
rationale.B: Concealed sequence, matched oils and carryover testing; incomplete follow-up and self-reported background diet remain.
rationale.P: CI narrows direction; clinical and neuronal significance not established.
rationale.R: EUROLIVE multicentre design and later subgroup papers remain one dataset; no independent replication credit assigned.

six_atoms.Intervention: 25 mL/day (22 g) raw olive oil replacing other raw fats; 366 versus 2.7 mg/kg phenolics, with intermediate 164 mg/kg arm; three weeks each, two-week washouts.

moa.description: Phenolic compounds may limit lipid oxidation; this trial does not isolate individual compounds or prove NF-κB modulation.
moa.status: Proposed relationship; measured endpoint does not establish causal mediation

Biological relationship.measuredEffect: Oxidised LDL changed −3.21 U/L (95% CI −5.1 to −0.8) with high phenolics; dose trend supported. F2-isoprostanes did not vary significantly by phenolic exposure.
Biological relationship.pmRelevance: Peripheral lipid-oxidation evidence supports a bounded PM5 relationship, not demonstrated neuronal membrane protection.

records.first_line: Six-minute guided breathing after a speech stressor → higher recovery RMSSD

source.context: Plans et al. (2019); 75 participants; random assignment; blinded ECG artifact review; non-preregistered pilot.

limitations.text: No verified six-breaths/minute prescription; remove that preliminary-discovery shorthand.
Table 1 does not show significant HF difference versus passive control; narrative overgeneralisation is not adopted.
Monitoring ended after six minutes; breathing itself affects HRV.
Developer employees authored study; editorial notice flags nonregistration. No cardiovascular-disease prevention claim.

rationale.D: Direct ECG RMSSD during specified recovery window.
rationale.B: Randomised controls and blinded artifact handling; unregistered pilot and sponsor interests limit protection.
rationale.P: SD and group statistics support bounded direction, not durability or clinical magnitude.
rationale.R: One empirical pilot for this combined app/breathing protocol.

six_atoms.Intervention: Six minutes of app-guided Papworth–Benson diaphragmatic breathing with heart-wave feedback versus passive control or rumination after a laboratory speech stressor.
six_atoms.Intervention type: Lifestyle Lever — Stress and autonomic regulation

moa.description: Respiratory modulation of cardiac intervals may contribute; vagal mediation was not isolated.
moa.status: Proposed relationship; measured endpoint does not establish causal mediation

Biological relationship.measuredEffect: Recovery RMSSD 65.9 versus39.88 ms in passive control; group P=.001. Heart-rate group P=.08; subjective stress recovered in all arms.
Biological relationship.pmRelevance: A short autonomic-recovery marker fits PM6, without proving durable parasympathetic recovery.

records.first_line: Tested evening blue-blocking glasses → earlier salivary melatonin onset

source.context: Liset et al. (2022); nulliparous third-trimester women;60 analysed,47 usable onset estimates; home saliva sampling; baseline-adjusted ANCOVA.

limitations.text: Onset estimation excluded out-of-range samples; baseline and follow-up counts differ.
Pregnancy-specific, not universal sleep treatment.
Transient malaise and other symptoms reported; one control participant withdrew for severe malaise.
Not standard dim-light laboratory onset; comparator also filters blue light.

rationale.D: Direct salivary threshold-onset outcome under exact tested conditions.
rationale.B: Randomised masked glasses; home collection and selected measurable samples remain concerns.
rationale.P: CI spans5–51 minutes; no validated clinical adequacy threshold.
rationale.R: One pregnancy dataset; healthy-adult sleep studies test another endpoint.

six_atoms.Intervention: Uvex S1933X glasses blocking 99% below530nm, from three hours before bedtime and during nocturnal light exposure for two weeks; compare partial-blocking S1905 glasses.

moa.description: Short-wavelength filtering reduces retinal light exposure; the measured onset under exposure cannot separate acute suppression relief from persistent clock phase shifting.
moa.status: Proposed relationship; measured endpoint does not establish causal mediation

Biological relationship.measuredEffect: Adjusted melatonin-onset difference28 minutes (95% CI5–51); bedtime, sleep onset and phase angles did not differ significantly.
Biological relationship.pmRelevance: Light input and melatonin timing relate to entrainment; sustained phase shift and better sleep are not established.

records.first_line: Six-month calorie restriction → higher muscle mitochondrial-DNA content

source.context: Civitarese et al. (2007);36 healthy overweight adults,12 per arm;11 paired molecular samples per arm; molecular outcomes not prespecified.

limitations.text: Marker change must not be relabelled improved mitochondrial respiration.
Weight and fat-free mass fell; not a general-population restriction prescription.
Small exploratory molecular analysis; multiple endpoints and unblinded exposure.
No brain-energy, longevity or ADHD benefit established.

rationale.D: Exact muscle mtDNA observation measured by qPCR.
rationale.B: Randomisation and weight-maintenance control; nonprespecified molecular outcomes limit protection.
rationale.P: SEM supports a marker signal; small samples and null enzyme results constrain magnitude/meaning.
rationale.R: One pilot dataset; separate cell experiments are not human replication.

six_atoms.Intervention: 25% energy restriction for six months versus weight-maintenance control; separate12.5% restriction plus12.5% exercise arm not pooled.

moa.description: Energy deficit may engage biogenesis-associated transcription; cellular nitric-oxide experiments do not demonstrate mediation in participants.
moa.status: Proposed relationship; measured endpoint does not establish causal mediation

Biological relationship.measuredEffect: Muscle mtDNA increased35±5% in restriction arm; citrate-synthase protein and tested mitochondrial enzyme activities did not increase.
Biological relationship.pmRelevance: mtDNA and transcription are biogenesis-associated markers, not direct organelle counts or increased respiratory capacity.
